title: Worldseed a procedural fantasy world
author: niklasdaking
selftext:
**Worldseed** generates an entire world from its name - its people, settlements, wilderness, and music. You land in that world and explore it.

*Massive update*

This update focuses on making that world larger, deeper, and more connected.

**The great city**

The city's diameter has doubled, with four ring streets and nearly four times as many buildings. There are markets with named stalls and traders, three taverns, a cathedral, a keep, and a watch that patrols at night.

The city is part of the world itself. You can see it from a distance, approach along the road, and walk through the gate without a loading screen or a separate map. Its districts are drawn around the player so the city can run on a phone.

**Underground locations**

* Crypts beneath burial mounds, with grave goods, inscriptions, and dead lords who rise if disturbed.
* Cellars beneath houses, sometimes hiding older vaults and maps to places you haven't found.
* Three-level mazes beneath stone circles, with dead ends, abandoned camps, and a keeper waiting at the bottom.

**Named beasts**

Each world can have up to three named beasts living in the wilderness near settlements. The townsfolk know their stories, their territory is marked on your map, and killing one leaves it dead.

The goal behind these changes is to make the world feel continuous and persistent: the city isn't a separate level, the dungeon isn't just a combat room, and the wilderness has creatures the inhabitants already know about.

**Play Worldseed free in your browser:** [https://generic-king.itch.io/worldseed](https://generic-king.itch.io/worldseed)

It's been a substantial update, and I'm looking forward to seeing how people explore the new world.

comments.author: IamVeryBraves
comments.body: It's really not your fault, I am very sensitive to flickering and prone to motion sickness. So I am not the right demographic. But I'm a sucker for procedurally generated content, I think this is cool as hell, but it's not for me.
